chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, through his chain, elevating it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), who said:

The intellect is divided into three parts. Whoever possesses all of them has perfected his intellect, and whoever does not possess them has no intellect at all: good recognition of God, the Mighty and Exalted; good obedience to Him; and good patience with His command.
ai.seo_question: What are the three components of the intellect according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a foundational definition of 'aql, framing it not merely as cognitive reasoning but as a triad of gnosis (ma'rifah), obedience (ita'), and patience (sabr). This structure reflects the Shia emphasis on the integration of theoretical knowledge and practical piety, where intellectual perfection is validated by one's submission to divine will and endurance through trials.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-58 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Khalid who linked it up through a chain of narrators to God’s Prophet (MGB) who said, “

The intellect is divided into three parts. Whoever possesses all parts has perfected his intellect. Whoever doesn’t possess all parts has no intellect at all. These parts of intellect are having a good recognition of the Honorable the Exalted God, good obedience to God, and good recognition of His Orders .”
